title: Evaluating the Generalizability and Explainability of Firn Image Classification with Topological Features
description:
arXiv:2504.16150v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In this paper we evaluate the performance of topological features for generalizable and explainable classification of firn image data, with the broader goal of understanding the advantages, pitfalls, and trade-offs in topological featurization. Firn refers to layers of granular snow within glaciers that haven't yet been compressed into ice. This compaction process imposes distinct topological and geometric structure on firn that varies with depth within the firn column. However, the limited and highly correlated training data available results in naive classifiers (such as convolutional neural networks) overfitting to orientation-dependent features. This motivates us to evaluate topological data analysis (TDA) as a way to design features which capture the shape of the firn data while retaining a large degree of invariance. We evaluate two classes of topological features, sublevel set features and distance transform features, together with persistence curves, to predict sample depth from firn images. A range of challenging training-test scenarios reveals that no one choice of method dominates in all categories. In particular, we see a tradeoff between accuracy on the one hand, and generalizability and explainability (via feature importance) on the other.
